text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The European Union Summit in Amsterdam failed to agree on how the organization will function when new members are accepted.
- The finance police carried out searches in the house of the president of lithuania's soccer federation, Vytautas Dirmeikis.
- Much attention will be paid to European integration during a meeting with President Algirdas Brazauskas, Polish President Aleksandr Kwasniewski told the newspaper in an interview.
- Lithuania's oil refinery Mazheikiu Nafta started to eye Ukrainian market and intends to start construction of filling stations there.
- Officials dismissed allegations from Latvia that the Butinge oil terminal may be an enviromental threat.
- Wrigley and Dandy Chewing Gum have around 90 percent of the Lithuanian chewing gum market.
- The board of the stock exchange suspended temporarily the operations of Tauras Bank brokerage house on the bourse after its activities were halted.
- Mazheikiu Nafta oil refinery opened this week its sixth filling station in Lithuania.
- Top officials gave state awards to members of the womens basketball team who won gold medals at the European championship.
- Polish parliament approved on Wednesday the foundation of an interparliamentary assembly with Lithuania.
- The government decided to impose a ceiling on the salaries of the managers of state-run companies.
